model: TEC26x6(H)-2 Series Fan Coil Thermostat with Dehumidification and Three Fan Speeds (BACnet MS/TP)
applies_to: Two- or four-pipe fan coils and cabinet unit heaters with three fan speeds, using the older TEC26x6(H)-2 thermostats.
summary: The TEC26x6(H)-2 is the earlier generation of the TEC fan coil thermostat on BACnet MS/TP. Its instance numbers differ from the later TEC26x6(H)-4. The list covers system mode, fan mode, occupancy, occupied/unoccupied setpoints, loop demands, auxiliary output, valve and fan status, input status, alarms and configuration; humidity objects exist only on the TEC2636 and TEC2656 models.
notes: Objects from Table 2 (MS/TP Bus Objects) on pages 7-11 of the installation instructions.
Access comes from the guide's footnotes: read/write, read-only, or writable only after the matching override object is set to Override.
The device object (instance 73aaa, aaa = MS/TP address) is not listed as a point.
Temperatures are listed in °F; the guide also gives the °C range.

source.title: TEC26x6(H)-2 Series BACnet MS/TP Networked Thermostats with Two Outputs, Dehumidification Capability, and Three Speeds of Fan Control Installation Instructions

integration.summary: Address the thermostat on the BACnet MS/TP trunk, then command System Mode (MV 13) and Occupancy (MV 12) and Fan Mode (MV 14) and write the occupied setpoints (AV 49/50). Read Room Temp, Fan Status and the filter and service alarms.

minimum_points.name: System Mode
minimum_points.why: System mode: off, cool, heat or auto

minimum_points.name: Fan Mode
minimum_points.why: Fan mode; states follow Fan Mode Sequence

integration.enable: Occupancy (MV 12) set to Occupied, Unoccupied or Temporary Occupied overrides the thermostat; Resume Schedule hands occupancy back. System Mode (MV 13) can switch the unit off.
integration.heartbeat: All network overrides are released automatically after 10 minutes without communication to any other device (for example if the network cable is removed). Keep the thermostat on an active trunk and rewrite overrides if needed.
integration.remote_sensors: To supply room temperature from the BAS, set Room Temp Override (BV 7) to Override and write Room Temp (AV 6). Outdoor Temperature (AV 8) is only valid when it is written over the network.
setup: BACnet MS/TP only; set the MS/TP address (4 to 127) at the thermostat.
The thermostat names itself TEC26x6-aaa and picks device instance 73aaa, where aaa is the MS/TP address (e.g. 73004). Change either before mapping points if needed.
Use automatic baud detection on the thermostat; the supervisory controller should hold a fixed baud rate.
Max_Master in the device object is writable.
gotchas: Only one override is active per object, and the last override command wins; a network override disables local adjustment of that object.
Writing one setpoint of a heating/cooling pair can make the thermostat move the other one to keep the minimum deadband.
These -2 instance numbers do not match the TEC26xx-4 generation; rediscover objects after a replacement.
Objects with no access mark in the guide are listed here as read-only.
